one_liner: Python ccache-style object cache for MSVC cl.exe that skips recompiling unchanged translation units on repeat builds.
what_it_does: clcache is invoked in place of cl.exe (CLCACHE_CL or PATH lookup, a CMake compiler launcher, or MSBuild's CLToolExe/CLToolPath). For a single-source /c compile it returns a previously stored .obj plus the captured compiler stdout/stderr when the inputs match, and relays everything else (linking, /Zi, /Yc or /Yu precompiled headers, /E /EP /P preprocessing) to the real compiler unchanged. It is a drop-in wrapper rather than a build system; the CLI only adds cache management (-s stats, -c trim, -C clear, -z reset, -M max size). Storage is a local directory (default %HOME%\clcache) or a memcached backend.
how_it_is_fast: Content-addressed result caching, modeled on ccache. In the default direct mode an MD5 of the compiler binary's mtime and size, the normalized command line and the source file selects a manifest; on a miss clcache injects /showIncludes to record the header set, and on later runs a hit only requires the MD5 of every recorded header to match, so the preprocessor is not run (CLCACHE_NODIRECT falls back to hashing /EP output). A hit copies, or with CLCACHE_HARDLINK hard-links, the stored object instead of compiling. The optional clcachesrv server keeps header hashes in memory and watches the files for changes; the maintainer found warm-cache time dominated by hashing include files (issue #239), which is the cost the server targets.
when_to_use: Windows CI jobs with MSVC where a restored cache directory covers most translation units (OpenMW's draft MR saw 100 then 55 minutes on the 2nd and 3rd cached runs of a job that otherwise sits near its 2 hour timeout).
Developer machines that rebuild the same sources after cleans or branch switches with the same compiler install and build directory (or CLCACHE_BASEDIR set).
Ninja, NMake or CMake compiler-launcher builds, or MSBuild builds that can run with TrackFileAccess=false (required for MSBuild cache hits per the wiki).
Codebases that can compile with /Z7 instead of /Zi and without MSVC precompiled headers, since those invocations bypass the cache.
when_not_to_use: Cold or mostly-miss builds: upstream issue reports show the empty-cache build slower than no cache (4:49 to 6:22 on a 4-core CI machine in #239; 7 to 23 minutes in #251), so one-off builds lose.

Projects that depend on /Zi PDBs or PCH (/Yc, /Yu): those compiles are passed through uncached, and switching to /Z7 and turning PCH off to get hits can slow the uncached build and enlarge objects and the cache.

Current toolchains with upstream code: the archived repository predates Python 3.10 and MSVC 2019 flags such as /external:I, and users run forks pinned to a commit (OpenMW used Aussiemon/clcache@21c50c2).

Very large or highly parallel builds: CacheLockException timeouts on section and stats locks and slow in-build cache cleanup are open, unfixed issues (#251, #347; one reporter's cache passed 100 GB and a million files).
Non-Windows hosts or GCC/Clang command lines: it uses Win32 named mutexes and only parses cl.exe/clang-cl options; sccache or ccache cover those.

integration.form: module (Python package exposing clcache and clcache-server console scripts; optional PyInstaller-built executable)
integration.dependencies: Python 3 with atomicwrites, pymemcache and pyuv (setup.py install_requires); the real cl.exe; optional memcached server
integration.min_toolchain: Python 3.5+ upstream (CI tested 3.5 and 3.6; 3.3/3.4 dropped in 4.2.0); MSVC tested in CI with Visual Studio 2013; Python >=3.10 and MSVC >=2019 need third-party fork patches
integration.platforms: Windows only (Win32 named mutexes and named pipes via ctypes windll)
integration.thread_safety: Concurrent invocations on one machine coordinate through Windows named mutexes in the Local\ namespace: hash-sharded locks for object and manifest sections (256 sections per the maintainer in #251) plus a global statistics lock, with a 10 s default timeout (CLCACHE_OBJECT_CACHE_TIMEOUT_MS). These do not coordinate across machines sharing a cache directory.
integration.drop_in_for_baseline: partial — wraps cl.exe transparently, but only single-source /c compiles without /Zi or PCH are cached, and MSBuild needs TrackFileAccess=false to get hits

gotchas: The compiler is identified by cl.exe's mtime and size, not its contents, so reinstalling or re-imaging the same MSVC version can invalidate the whole cache.
Changes to the INCLUDE and LIBPATH environment variables are not detected in direct mode and can return a stale object (wiki Caveats); set CLCACHE_NODIRECT or clear the cache.
CLCACHE_COMPRESS caches are incompatible with uncompressed ones; changing the setting requires clearing the cache.
clcachesrv watches header directories and blocks deleting them (use its exclude option), and a PyInstaller --onefile build is documented as considerably slower.
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Pick clcache over sccache only for an MSVC-only Windows build that needs no remote storage and already runs a pinned fork; sccache is maintained, handles MSVC as well as GCC/Clang/Rust/CUDA and offers shared cloud backends. Against FASTBuild or octobuild it needs no build-system change, but it caches nothing the build does not pass as a plain /c compile.
verified_claims_summary: The only recent numbers come from OpenMW's unmerged draft MR !5021: a GitLab Windows MSBuild RelWithDebInfo job (MSVC 2022, 64-bit, runner hardware not stated) that usually sits at its 2 hour timeout uncached finished in 100, 55 and as little as 49 minutes on successive runs with a restored cache, using a patched fork rather than upstream, and with precompiled headers turned off (OpenMW's CMake default is on), /Zi rewritten to /Z7 and MSBuild TrackFileAccess disabled only in the cached configuration, so the ~2.2x (derived from page data, against the timeout) compares different builds across separate pipelines. Upstream issue #239 has a same-machine user measurement of upstream clcache: 4:49 without, 6:22 cold and 2:06 warm on a 4-core 2 GHz SSD CI machine (about 2.3x warm, derived from page data), and 2:21 against 1:10 warm on a 4-core 3.3 GHz machine; project and compiler version not stated.
status_note: Archived by its owner on 2020-02-04 with the last upstream commit on 2019-02-19; BSD-3-Clause and pure Python, so it can be vendored, but modern Python and MSVC need a third-party fork such as Aussiemon/clcache, whose 2025 commits add Python >=3.10 and /external:I fixes.
